1  COMMON JUDGMENT  1. These petitions have arisen out of the same accident and therefore, they are taken up together for disposal by this common judgment.
 2. MVC No.3754/2018 has been filed by the petitioner seeking compensation of Rs.25 lakhs for the death of his wife Smt.G.Mamatha, MVC No.3755/2018 seeking compensation of Rs.10 lakhs for the death of his son G.Lohith and Mvc No.3756/2018 seeking compensation of Rs.10 lakhs for the injuries suffered by him in the motor vehicle accident which occurred on 13.05.2018 at about 03.45 pm., on NH 42 Road, Kaigal  SCCH 1 3 MVC 3754, 3755 & 3756/2018 Village, Baireddipalle Mandal, Chittoor District, Andhra Pradesh.
 3.
The brief facts of the case are that:-

On 13.05.2018, the petitioner as rider with his wife deceased G.Mamatha and his deceased son G.Lohith as pillion riders, was travelling on Motorcycle No.AP.03/B.9407 from Baireddypalle Village towards V.Kota with care and caution on the left side of the road.

At about 03.45 pm., when they reached near Kaigal Village on NH 42 Road, Baireddipalle Mandal,
Chittoor District, a lorry bearing registration No.AP.03/TD.9390 driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life and (Common Sri Damodara vs ) M/S.Plr Projects Pvt on 29 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187016359/

safety of others came from opposite direction and dashed against their motorcycle.
As a result of the terrible impact, petitioner, his wife and son sustained grievous injuries.
4. It is the further case of the petitioner that his wife G.Mamatha succumbed to the injuries at PES Hospital, Kuppam while undergoing treatment.
After post mortem, the petitioner has performed the last rites by incurring huge expenses.
The deceased was aged 30 years at the time of the accident and working as tailor and earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
On account of her untimely death, he has been put to untold hardship and misery and hence, has claimed a compensation of Rs.25 lakhs from the respondents.
5. It is the further case of the petitioner that in the accident, his son G.Lohith sustained grievous injuries and died at the spot.
After post mortem, he has performed the last rites.
At the time of the accident, his son was aged 7 years.

On account of death of his son in the accident, he has suffered severe mental agony and hardship and hence, he has claimed a  SCCH 1 5 MVC 3754, 3755 & 3756/2018 compensation of Rs.10 lakhs from the respondents.

The gist of the contentions taken by the respondent No.2 in all the petitions is that:
 The Petitions are not maintainable for want of jurisdiction.
It is for the petitioner to prove that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent  SCCH 1 7 MVC 3754, 3755 & 3756/2018 driving of the lorry No.AP.03/TD.9390 .

It is contended that the petitioner in MVC No.3756/2018 who was riding the motorcycle is guilty of contributory negligence and as such, the petitioner is not entitled to claim compensation from the respondents either jointly or severally.
It is for the petitioner to prove that G.Mamatha and G.Lohith died on account of the injuries and the petitioner in MVC No.3756/2018 suffered grievous injuries in the accident.
The petitions are bad for non joinder of necessary parties ie., the owner and insurer of the Motorcycle No.AP.03/B.9407.
It is for the petitioner and 1st respondent to prove that the lorry No.AP.03/TD.9390 was insured with it as the issuance of insurance policy to the said vehicle is yet to be confirmed.

Without prejudice to the said contentions,
the respondent No.2 has contended that it is not aware of the correctness or otherwise of the averments in Column No.1 to 6 of the petition about the age,

Therefore, though the petitioner being a legal heir is entitled to compensation,
but he is not entitled to compensation under the head of loss of dependency.
In the said circumstances, the question that arises is under what head the petitioner would be entitled to compensation.

In this regard it is useful to the refer to the decision of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the case of A.Manavalagan Vs A.Krishnamurthy and others (ILR 2004 KAR 3268 =
2005 ACJ 992).

The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the said decision while summarizing the principles for  SCCH 1 20 MVC 3754, 3755 & 3756/2018 determining the compensation where the claimant is not a dependent has held as follows:-
 "19.

We may summarize the principles enunciated,
thus:-
(i) xxxxxxx (ii) xxxxxx (iii) Where the claim by the legal representatives of the deceased who were not dependents of the deceased

,
then the basis for award of compensation is the loss to the estate, that is the loss of savings by the deceased.
A conventional sum for loss of expectation of life, is added.
(iv) the procedure for determination of loss to estate is broadly the same as the procedure for determination of the loss of dependency.
Both involve ascertaining the multiplicand and capitalizing it by multiplying it by a appropriate multiplier.

But, the significant difference is in the figure arrived at as multiplicant in the cases where the claimants who are dependents claim loss of dependency and in cases where the claimants who are (Common Sri Damodara vs ) M/S.Plr Projects Pvt on 29 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187016359/
14 not dependents claim loss to estate.

The annual  SCCH 1 21 MVC 3754, 3755 & 3756/2018 contribution to the family constitutes the multiplicand in the case of loss of dependency, where as the annual savings of the deceased becomes the multiplicant in the case of loss to estate.
The method of selection of multiplier is however the same in both cases.
20. xxxxxxxxxx (I) xxxxxxx
( ii) xxxxxx (iii) xxxxxx
Note; xxxxx (iv) xxxxx
(v) xxxxx

Though the quantum of savings will vary from person to person, there is a need to standardize the quantum of savings for determining the loss of estate (where the claimants are not dependents) in the absence of specific evidence to the contrary.
The quantum of savings can be taken as one third of the income of the deceased where the spouses are having a common establishment and 1/4th where the spouses are having independent establishments.
The above will apply  SCCH 1 22 MVC 3754, 3755 & 3756/2018 where the family consists of non dependent spouse/children/parents.
Where the claimants are non dependent brothers/ sisters claiming on behalf of the estate, the savings can be taken as 15% of the income.
The above percentages, one of course, subject to any specific evidence to the contrary led by the claimants".

Hence, 1/3rd of Rs.21,50,400/- works out to Rs.7,16,800/- which the petitioner is entitled under the head loss to estate.

It is the case of the petitioner that in the accident, he sustained grievous injuries and was treated as inpatient in PES  SCCH 1 26 MVC 3754, 3755 & 3756/2018 Hospital, Kuppam and thereafter, at R.L.Jalappa Hospital, Kolar.

In all the cases, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount and the respondent No.2 shall indemnify the respondent No.1 and pay the compensation to the petitioner within 2 months from the date of this order.

50% of the compensation amount with proportionate interest, in all the cases, is ordered to be invested in high yielding FD in the name of the petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of his choice for a period of 5 years and the remaining amount with proportionate interest is ordered to be released to the petitioner.
Interest on FD is payable on maturity.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- in each case.
Original judgment shall be kept in MVC No.3754/2018 and its copies in other cases.
